children: Egypt’s renewable energy capacity increased by 21 percent in 2025 to 9,366 megawatts (MW) from about 7,752MW in 2024, local Arabic financial news portal Alborsa reported on Thursday.

The report, citing data from the Central Agency for Public Mobilisation and Statistics (CAPMAS), said renewable energy capacity has increased by about 156 percent over the past decade, from 3,658MW in 2015 to 9,366MW in 2025.
The increase reflects Egypt's expansion of renewable power generation as the country seeks to diversify its energy mix and increase the use of lower-emission sources.

Egypt has also expanded the use of natural gas as a vehicle fuel, according to CAPMAS. The number of vehicles converted to run on natural gas reached about 562,000 at the end of fiscal year 2024/2025, compared with 555,300 a year earlier.
(Writing by Majda Muhsen; Editing by Anoop Menon)
